subject: General Knowledge
topic: Awards & Honors — major international and national awards

questions.stem: Which is the highest civilian award in India?

options.option_text: Padma Shri
Bharat Ratna
Padma Bhushan
Ashoka Chakra

questions.explanation: Bharat Ratna: highest civilian award in India. Given for service of highest order. Answer: B. Trap: A (third), C (second), D (military/bravery).

questions.stem: The Nobel Prize in Physics is awarded for:

options.option_text: Outstanding achievement in medical research
Outstanding contribution to physics science
Excellence in engineering (alternative interpretation)
Achievement in environmental conservation

questions.explanation: Nobel Prize in Physics: outstanding scientific discovery in physics. Established by Alfred Nobel's will. Answer: B. Trap: A (Physiology/Medicine), C (not Nobel category), D (not standard Nobel).

questions.stem: How many Padma awards are there?

options.option_text: 1 (Padma Shri only) (alternative interpretation)
2 (Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri) (alternative interpretation)
3 (Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri)
4 (additional Padma Deshik) (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: Padma awards (3 tiers): Padma Vibhushan (highest, exceptional), Padma Bhushan (distinguished), Padma Shri (meritorious service). Answer: C. Trap: A/B (incomplete), D (Padma Deshik not standard).

questions.stem: The Booker Prize is awarded for:

options.option_text: Outstanding contribution to science
Excellence in fiction writing
Achievement in poetry (alternative interpretation)
Excellence in journalism

questions.explanation: Booker Prize: prestigious award for fiction writing (English-language novels). Awarded annually since 1969. Answer: B. Trap: A (not Booker), C (not primarily poetry), D (journalism separate).

questions.stem: Which award is given for bravery in India?

options.option_text: Padma Shri (alternative interpretation)
Ashoka Chakra
Bharat Ratna
Param Veer Chakra

questions.explanation: Ashoka Chakra: highest peacetime medal for bravery/gallantry in India (civilian). Param Veer Chakra = military. Answer: B. Trap: A (civilian service), C (highest overall), D (military).

questions.stem: The Grammy Award is given for achievement in:

options.option_text: Cinema/Film industry
Music industry
Television industry
Visual arts

questions.explanation: Grammy Award: prestigious award for music recording achievement (American). Answer: B. Trap: A (Oscar/Academy Award), C (Emmy), D (visual arts awards differ).

questions.stem: The Turing Award is often called the 'Nobel Prize of Computing'. True or False?

options.option_text: True — it's the highest award in computer science
False — it's only for programming (alternative interpretation)
False — it's not internationally recognized
False — it's given by the Nobel Committee

questions.explanation: Turing Award: ACM's highest award, considered 'Nobel Prize of Computing' for outstanding contributions to computer science. Answer: A. Trap: B (broader scope), C (internationally prestigious), D (independent, not Nobel Committee).

questions.stem: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award, instituted in 1969, is India's highest official recognition for lifetime achievement in which domain?

options.option_text: Indian classical music and performing dance arts
Indian cinema and filmmaking as lifelong contribution
Indian literature and creative writing legacy
Indian folk art and traditional handicraft forms

questions.explanation: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is conferred at the National Film Awards ceremony for outstanding contribution to the growth and development of Indian cinema. Option A is tempting because performing arts are closely linked to films, but the award is specifically restricted to cinema, not classical music or dance independently.

questions.stem: The Abel Prize in mathematics, established in 2003, is administered and funded by the government of which country?

options.option_text: Sweden, home of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
Germany, where Abel published his groundbreaking proofs
Norway, honouring mathematician Niels Henrik Abel
Denmark, the country where Abel spent his later years

questions.explanation: The Abel Prize is awarded by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters and funded by the Norwegian government, honouring Niels Henrik Abel (1802–1829), a Norwegian mathematician famous for proving the quintic equation has no general algebraic solution. Sweden is the most common wrong answer because Nobel Prizes — which lack a mathematics category — originate from Sweden.

questions.stem: The Dronacharya Award is conferred by the Government of India upon which category of individuals in the field of sports?

options.option_text: Sports scientists who develop advanced training techniques for athletes
Sports coaches who produce medal-winning athletes at major international events
Former champions who serve as mentors in national sports academies
Sports administrators who organise national and international competitions

questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award recognises coaches who have successfully trained athletes to win medals at prestigious international events such as the Olympics, Asian Games, or Commonwealth Games. Option C (former champions as mentors) is a common distractor; the award requires coaches to have demonstrated concrete medal-winning outcomes, not merely a mentoring role.

questions.stem: The Kalinga Prize, awarded by UNESCO since 1952, specifically recognises an individual's outstanding work in which field?

options.option_text: Preservation of world cultural heritage sites globally
Popularisation of science and technology for the general public
Advancement of climate-change awareness in developing countries
Development of universal literacy in newly independent nations

questions.explanation: The Kalinga Prize is awarded for making science and technology accessible and engaging to the general public — through writing, lecturing, broadcasting, or digital media. It was established with a donation from Biju Patnaik, former Chief Minister of Odisha. Option A (heritage preservation) is frequently confused with other UNESCO prizes such as the Melina Mercouri International Prize.

questions.stem: The Jawaharlal Nehru Award for International Understanding, instituted in 1965 by the Indian Council for Cultural Relations, is given for outstanding contribution to:

options.option_text: Scientific research of global significance and humanitarian impact
Promotion of international peace and goodwill among peoples
Literature that fosters dialogue across civilisations and faiths
Economic development in newly independent and developing countries

questions.explanation: The Jawaharlal Nehru Award for International Understanding is presented to individuals or organisations for promoting international peace, understanding, and goodwill. Past recipients include U Thant, Martin Luther King Jr., and Julius Nyerere. Option C (literature) is a plausible wrong answer because Nehru was himself a celebrated writer, but this award is not literary in scope.

questions.stem: The Param Vir Chakra medal's circular design features four replicas of a specific weapon drawn from Hindu mythology. Which weapon appears on the medal?

options.option_text: Trishul (trident) of Lord Shiva, the destroyer deity
Sudarshana Chakra (discus) of Lord Vishnu the preserver
Vajra (thunderbolt) of Indra, the king of the devas
Pinaka (bow) of Lord Rama, the warrior avatar of Vishnu

questions.explanation: The Param Vir Chakra, India's highest wartime gallantry decoration, was designed by Savitri Khanolkar (née Eva de Maday). The medal features four replicas of the Vajra — Indra's thunderbolt — symbolising invincible power. The Trishul (option A) is the most frequent wrong choice because it is the most widely recognised Hindu symbol, but Shiva's weapon has no connection to this medal's iconography.

questions.stem: The International Booker Prize, which is distinct from the standard Booker Prize, is awarded annually for the best work of:

options.option_text: Debut fiction by a non-English-speaking first-time author
Fiction translated into English and published in the UK or Ireland
Any novel by a Commonwealth or Republic of Ireland citizen
Short fiction and novellas published in the United Kingdom

questions.explanation: The International Booker Prize (formerly the Man Booker International Prize) recognises a single work of fiction translated into English and published in the UK or Ireland; the prize money is split equally between the author and translator. Option C describes the older citizenship-based eligibility rules of the standard Booker Prize, making it the most tempting distractor for those who conflate the two awards.
